The player moved from col 20-22 to col 14-16 with a single LEFT action. That's a big jump — 6 columns? Wait, the player's b was at c 15-16, and Y was at c 14. Previously b was at c 20-21, and Y was at c 22. So the player moved about 5-6 columns to the left with a single LEFT. Interesting — either the player is sliding until it hits a wall, or it's moving at high speed.
Wait, actually the player might be moving until it hits an obstacle. The left edge of the S region is col 13. The player is now at cols 14-16 (Y is at col 14, b is at cols 15-16). Hmm, Y is on the left side now (facing left). The left boundary of the S region is col 13 (B is at col 12). So the player slid all the way to the left wall.
So LEFT/RIGHT moves the player until it hits a wall (slide to the edge). Or maybe the player moves at a fixed speed of 6 per action? Let me test: I'll try RIGHT from the current position and see where it ends up.
Actually, wait — the player might be moving continuously until it hits a wall. The S region at rows 37-40 spans cols 13-53. But there's a black band at rows 30-33. The player is at rows 37-40, below the band. The left wall is col 13 (B is at col 12). The player's leftmost pixel (Y) is at col 14, so it stopped 1 column away from the wall.
Let me test RIGHT and see where it stops — if it slides all the way to the right wall (col 53), then the movement is "slide to the wall." If it moves 6 columns, then it's fixed-speed movement.
